subject: Chemistry
title: Activated Charcoal: The Universal Antidote
description: A 60-second lesson on Activated Charcoal: The Universal Antidote.

hook.text: Swallow poison? Hospitals give you activated charcoal. It traps toxins before your gut can absorb them.

buildup.text: Activated charcoal is regular charcoal treated with heat and gas to create millions of tiny pores.

discovery.text: One gram has a surface area of 3,000 m²—a football field of adsorption surface in a tiny amount.

twist.text: It doesn't work on everything. Alcohols, acids, lithium, and iron pass right through without binding.

climax.text: In 1831, a chemist swallowed a lethal dose of strychnine mixed with charcoal in front of an audience. He survived.

punchline.text: Traps poisons in microscopic pores before the gut absorbs them. Simple and effective.

quiz.question: How does activated charcoal work as an antidote?
options: Its huge surface area adsorbs toxins in the gut before absorption
It speeds up the liver's detoxification process

details.summary: Activated charcoal has an enormous surface area of up to 3,000 square meters per gram that adsorbs ingested toxins in the gastrointestinal tract, preventing absorption into the bloodstream. It is the most widely used emergency decontaminant for oral poisonings worldwide.
details.whyItMatters: Activated charcoal is available in every hospital emergency department and reduces mortality from many types of oral poisoning. Its simplicity and broad effectiveness make it a cornerstone of toxicological emergency care.
takeaways: Activated charcoal binds toxins through physical adsorption in the gut
It must be administered within one to two hours of poison ingestion
It does not work against all poisons, notably metals and alcohols

faq.question: What poisons is activated charcoal ineffective against?
faq.answer: Activated charcoal does not effectively adsorb metals like iron and lithium, alcohols like ethanol and methanol, strong acids and bases, or petroleum products. It also has limited effectiveness against cyanide. These substances require specific antidotes or other treatments.

faq.question: How does activated charcoal differ from regular charcoal?
faq.answer: Activated charcoal is processed at extremely high temperatures with oxidizing gases to create a highly porous microstructure. One gram has the surface area of a tennis court. Regular charcoal has far less porosity and adsorptive capacity, making it medically ineffective.
